metadata.score_guide: HOW TO READ SUITABILITY SCORES. Every site has one score between 0 and 1, and higher is better. The score rewards three things: how built-up the area around the site is, which stands in for how many people are there (this counts for the most); how close the site is to a road; and how far it is from the nearest health facility that already exists, since a site far from one is filling a real gap. The score then goes down where the site is exposed to flooding, landslides or storm surge. Hazard is built into every score. There is no hazard-free view of the map, because a facility that cannot stay open during a disaster fails exactly when it is needed most. Scores compare sites within Talomo District only: a score of 1.00 means the best value seen in this district, not a perfect site in any absolute sense, and the scores would need to be recalculated to compare against another district. Road access is scored so that higher means closer — a reading near 0 means the site is FAR from the road network and would be hard to reach. Two rules can rule a site out no matter how well it scores: sitting within 50 m of the shoreline, or carrying a High rating on flood, landslide or storm surge. Sites ruled out this way are still shown, with the reason given, so you can see what was set aside and why.

dataset_clarification.note: Raw OSM records are the elements extracted for feature engineering — building footprints, road segments, existing health facilities and coastline. Candidate sites are the grid points scored by the model. The two figures count different things and are not comparable.

metadata.advisory_note: POLARIS is an advisory decision-support tool; final siting decisions remain with planning officers.
